destination.name: Nadi
destination.tagline: A Viti Levu base for temples, markets, mud pools and island ferries
destination.description: Nadi is the Viti Levu city that serves as the base for Denarau and the ferries to the Mamanuca and Yasawa islands. At its southern end the Sri Siva Subramaniya Temple is a large Dravidian-style Hindu temple that visitors can enter. The Sabeto valley has a mud bath and three hot-spring pools, and Viseisei is said to be the oldest settlement in Fiji. Behind the city, Koroyanitu National Heritage Park and the Nausori Highlands offer rainforest walks, and Lautoka, the next city north, has a large covered market.
whyVisit: Soak in hot springs and mud pools
Step inside a Dravidian-style Hindu temple

goodToKnow.title: Cover up at the temple
goodToKnow.detail: Visitors cover up to enter the Sri Siva Subramaniya Temple, so wear clothes that cover shoulders and knees.

goodToKnow.title: Island ferries leave Denarau
goodToKnow.detail: Boats to the Mamanuca and Yasawa islands go from Denarau, so plan your transfer around the sailing times.

goodToKnow.title: Carry small cash for villages
goodToKnow.detail: Viseisei Village charges an entry fee of about FJD 10, so keep small notes for village visits.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Visit in {months} for beach days, highland hikes and market visits. Cyclones can occur Nov to Apr.

nadi-1.bio: Orchid garden begun by actor Raymond Burr, with jungle walkways and lily ponds at the foot of the Sabeto Range.

nadi-2.bio: Large Dravidian-style Hindu temple at the southern end of Nadi, open to visitors who cover knees and shoulders.

nadi-3.bio: Mud bath followed by a circuit of three pools in the Sabeto valley, with massages available.

nadi-4.bio: Heritage park in the Mount Evans range behind Lautoka and Nadi, with guided hikes and waterfalls reached from Abaca village.

nadi-5.bio: Chiefly village near Lautoka, said to be Fiji's oldest settlement, founded where the first Melanesian canoes beached at Vuda Point.

nadi-6.bio: A 3 km beach north of Nadi town, lined with resorts and beach clubs.

nadi-7.bio: Fruit and vegetable market on Hospital Road in Nadi, selling cheap seasonal produce.

nadi-8.bio: Dry-zone mountain rainforest in Viti Levu's interior, with villages such as Navala and views, and a window onto Fijian culture.

nadi-9.bio: Large covered market beside Lautoka's bus station selling fruit, vegetables, spices and kava, with cooked-food stalls outside.
